body:
ACCEPT D3 AS A HARD CONSTRAINT. One additional amendment is load-bearing: the CLI output unit must be a build-result envelope, not only a serialized StoryModel[Validated].

Measured boundary today:

- StoryModel contains accepted story semantics and an optional core BuildReceipt. It does not contain the acquire CandidateLedger, proposal alternatives, rejected or unresolved states, or complete attempt history.
- ExtendedBuildReceipt is separate and its LayerCoverage currently distinguishes only NotAttempted from Attempted.
- StoryAtlas Edition.build accepts only StoryModel[Validated]. It then emits visual files plus receipt.json; it emits neither source nor model. It also currently assigns ViewBasis.ResearcherReviewedFixture inside the general build method.

Therefore a provider failure, unresolved candidate set, rejected high-impact claim, or validation failure cannot reach the current edition path. If the new CLI emits nothing graphical in those cases, the product violates D3 at exactly the failure boundary even if every successful model view is perfect.

I propose this law:

EVERY INVOCATION THAT CAN IDENTIFY AND CHECKSUM ITS INPUT EMITS AN AUDITABLE RESULT BUNDLE. A validated semantic model is optional in that envelope; the source, stage outcomes, requested and eligible universe, resolution states, diagnostics, and receipts are not optional merely because semantic validation failed.

This does not require weakening ViewCompiler or Edition.build. Keep the existing validated-model compiler strict. Add a sibling build-report renderer over a typed outcome envelope. On success it links to the normal Codex and Atlas artifacts. On partial or failed acquisition it renders the source plus addressable unresolved, absent, failed, ineligible, and excluded inventories, without minting graph claims or fake span anchors.

The other replies are right about raw bytes versus canonical UTF-16 text. I would add that the acquired versus researcher-reviewed basis must also be explicit: the current general Edition.build must not label arbitrary future CLI output ResearcherReviewedFixture.

Minimum courts unique to this boundary:

1. Provider failure after source intake still emits source, audit/result JSON, receipt, HTML report, and textual twin, but no counterfeit validated model.
2. Alternatives and Rejected survive the result round-trip and appear in the report even though they do not enter StoryModel.
3. Successful validation delegates to the existing validated Codex and Atlas compilers with an acquired/silver basis, never the fixture basis.
4. Remove one requested eligible address from both marks and disposition inventory: report certification refuses.
5. LayerCoverage Attempted with zero output cannot by itself decide Absent versus Failed versus Ineligible; the typed stage or resolution outcome must do so.

So my D2/D5 split is slightly wider: canonical storymodel JSON for accepted semantics, a canonical typed result or audit JSON for the acquisition account, deterministic HTML and text as reports, and explicitly lossy external exports. Whether those are two JSON files or one versioned envelope is wire design; collapsing the audit account into StoryModel is not.

Design disposition only. I created no bead and authorize no implementation.
